correctness.rationale: The source defines \(\psi\) by \(\psi(u)=u g(\psi(u))\), which immediately gives \(\psi(0)=0\). Lagrange inversion yields exactly the source's positive coefficients. Consul-Shenton's general formula shows that those coefficients correspond to \(f(z)=z\), hence zero mass \(f(0)=0\). Because the source's \(g\) is an offspring PGF, the coefficient sum is the smallest fixed point \(q=g(q)\), with the standard subcritical/critical versus supercritical extinction dichotomy. The packaged checker verifies the source's simulation example and a supercritical example.
